drainage.h1: Fixing wet backyards and soggy low spots in Henderson
drainage.lede: Rain stops at the clay under Henderson's sandy topsoil. We find where it goes, then fix it with the smallest solution that works.
drainage.answer: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned, fully insured company based in Longview that fixes yard drainage in Henderson. We are rated 5.0 on Google across {{REVIEWS}} reviews. We trace the water first, then regrade, reroute downspouts, cut swales or install French drains with sock-wrapped pipe and #57 stone. Small fixes run $450 to $1,000, and most Henderson drainage projects cost $2,000 to $3,750, with the price in writing after a free walkthrough.
local: Henderson's topsoil is sandy, and sand drinks water fast. Under it sits dense red clay. Rain soaks the top foot, hits the clay and stops. From there it pools in low spots or runs sideways toward the house. That is why low corners, flat backyards and beds against the slab are the places Henderson yards stay wet after a storm. The sand fools you, because the yard looks fine until the clay fills up.

We like to walk the property during or right after a rain, so we can see where the water comes from and where it sits. Then we start with the cheap fixes. Check the downspouts, check the grade, extend or reroute what is dumping at the foundation. A single problem spot, like a downspout reroute or one low spot, runs $450 to $1,000, and sometimes that is all it takes.

When the water needs more, the next steps are a swale, a pop-up emitter or a French drain. A drain is only as good as its outlet, so we dig with a steady fall toward somewhere the water can actually leave: daylight, a lower part of the lot, or a pop-up emitter. A standard single run costs $1,900 to $3,000, full systems $3,000 to $4,500, and combined projects with a wall or bed rebuild run $4,500 and up.

Cheap drains fail in this clay. Corrugated pipe in a rock bag, laid shallow with no real outlet, silts up in a season or two and has to be dug up again. We use sock-wrapped 4-inch perforated PVC set in #57 stone, backfilled with stone so clay fines cannot clog it, then cap the trench with sod or river rock. The digging is the expensive part, so we would rather do it once.

faq.q: Do you install French drains in Henderson?
faq.a: Yes, when a French drain is the right fix. We use sock-wrapped 4-inch perforated PVC set in #57 stone and tie it to a daylight outlet or a pop-up emitter. A standard single run usually costs $1,900 to $3,000, and sometimes a downspout reroute or a regrade solves the problem for less.

faq.q: Why does my Henderson backyard stay wet after a rain?
faq.a: Sandy topsoil over clay. Rain soaks in until it hits the clay, then it has nowhere to go. Flat backyards and low corners collect it, and new pads settle over time. We trace where the water comes from before we decide whether it needs a regrade, a swale or a drain.

faq.q: How much does drainage work cost in Henderson?
faq.a: Small fixes like a downspout reroute or one low spot run $450 to $1,000. Most projects cost $2,000 to $3,750. Full systems run $3,000 to $4,500, and large or combined projects start at $4,500. Linear feet, dig depth and the outlet decide where yours lands.

faq.q: Can you fix water pooling against my foundation?
faq.a: Often, yes. We check the downspouts and the grade first, then re-slope the ground away from the foundation, add a swale or run a drain to an outlet. You get a written, itemized estimate that says what we are installing and why.

faq.q: Do I really need a French drain?
faq.a: Not always. Sometimes a downspout extension or a regrade is enough, and we will say so. A French drain is the right call when water has to be collected and carried to an outlet, and we only recommend one when the water calls for it.

fertilization.local_h: Feeding a Henderson lawn when the pH is off
local: Fertilizer does very little when the soil is out of balance, and many Henderson lawns are. Years of pine needles and rain leave East Texas soil a little acidic, and an acidic lawn cannot use what you spread on it. That is why we pull a soil sample on bigger lawns before we put anything down. The test tells us whether the yard needs lime, and we add it only when the numbers say so. Guessing wastes money.

Most of the grass here splits two ways. Older Henderson lots under oaks and pines are St. Augustine, and the open and newer lots are mostly bermuda. They want different handling. On St. Augustine we hold the last real nitrogen for early September, because a heavy feeding in October fuels large patch right when nights turn cool and damp. October on shaded lawns is a potassium month. Bermuda gets its slow-release spring feeding once overnight lows hold above 60.

The first feeding goes down around April 25, not in March when the big-box stores start stacking bags. Soil in this part of Rusk County is still cold in March, and half-dormant grass cannot take it in, so the next rain washes it away. Then the plan runs through a summer-safe feeding in early July, an early September feeding to build roots, and the October winterizer. We write that schedule down before the first visit.

Sandy topsoil over clay packs down, especially on lots that see a lot of foot traffic and equipment. Compacted lawns get core aeration between late August and mid-September, with the feeding right behind it. Heavy shade is the one thing fertilizer cannot fix. If a St. Augustine patch under a big oak keeps thinning, we will tell you it needs light, not more bags, and we will say so on the walkthrough.

faq.q: Will lime help my Henderson lawn?
faq.a: Only if the soil test says so. Many East Texas yards run a little acidic from pine needles and rain, and lime brings the pH back up so fertilizer can do its job. We test on bigger jobs before adding anything, rather than guessing, and we show you what the numbers said.

faq.q: When should I fertilize in Henderson?
faq.a: The first feeding goes down around April 25, once overnight lows hold above 60 and the grass is fully awake. After that come early July, early September, and a potassium winterizer in late October. Feeding in March mostly washes out, because bermuda and St. Augustine cannot use it yet.

faq.q: What does a fertilization visit cost in Henderson?
faq.a: Visits start from about $190. Seasonal programs are priced on your lawn size, the grass type, how many rounds it needs, and whether you add lime or core aeration. You get the plan and the price in writing before the first application, so there are no surprises at the door.

faq.q: Does the program include weed or pest treatment?
faq.a: No. We do not do any weed or pest treatment. What we do is test the soil, feed on the right schedule, add lime when needed, aerate compacted lawns, and give you honest advice on mowing height and shade. A well-fed lawn mowed at the right height holds up better on its own.

faq.q: Can you fertilize a lawn that is thin under my oak trees?
faq.a: We can feed it, and the soil test tells us what it needs. But thin grass under heavy canopy is mostly short on light. We will be straight with you on the walkthrough about which spots will respond to feeding and which would do better as a shade bed or mulch.

In full sun we reach for knockout roses, salvia, lantana and plumbago, which hold up through August. Petunias and impatiens look good in April and are done by the Fourth of July, so that is a plant-choice problem, not a green-thumb one.

Before we pick a single plant, we look at how many hours of sun the bed gets and how it drains. In Henderson, the beds against the slab are the ones that hold water, since sandy topsoil sits over clay and rain stops at the clay. So every new bed gets a grade that moves water away from the house. A bed that stays wet will finish off plants whatever you put in it.

Prep comes first. We cut a clean edge in stone, steel or a natural cut, pull weeds by the root, loosen the top of the soil and work in compost where the clay is heavy. Plants go in with real spacing so air moves through them, and mulch goes down at an inch to an inch and a half, pulled back off the stems. That is the depth that works in our wet springs.

Timing helps too. Shrubs and perennials do best planted in fall, September through November, while the soil is warm and the air is cooling. Heat lovers like vinca should wait until mid-May or later. When we finish, we walk you through watering: deep and less often, so roots go down and do not rot in wet clay. If you want to see the bed drawn first, our Flower Bed Preview is $199.

faq.a: Usually it is the soil, not the plants. Compacted ground, beds that hold water, or mulch piled too deep will finish off plants in our heat. We fix the prep first, then plant for the sun the bed actually gets.

faq.q: What should I plant in a shady bed under pines and oaks?

hedge-trimming.local_h: Bringing back an old Henderson foundation hedge
local: Walk an older Henderson street and you will see the same hedge over and over. Hollies, ligustrums and photinias were planted along the foundation decades ago, then sheared flat across the top every year since. The top gets thick and shades the bottom, and the bottom goes bare and woody. We fix that by reshaping the hedge a little narrower at the top and wider at the base, so light reaches the lower branches and they keep their leaves.

Some of these hedges have grown past the windows or crowded the walk. Ligustrum and photinia usually take a hard rejuvenation cut well and fill back in over a season or two. Timing matters, so we plan the cut for when the plant will recover best, and we tell you on the walkthrough if a shrub is too far gone and better replaced. Hollies are forgiving and shape best in June, though a hard cut trims some of the winter berries.

Azaleas and camellias are the exception on those same beds. They set next year's buds soon after they finish blooming, so we trim them right after bloom and no later. Shearing them in fall or winter costs you next spring's flowers. Before we cut anything we count the shrubs and note which ones bloom on old wood, and that decides the order and the dates. A late cut is a common reason an old azalea bed goes without flowers.

Tarps go down under every hedge, and the cuttings are raked up, blown out of the beds and hauled away. Older lots with mature trees often have narrow beds along the house, so we work by hand, not with a big machine. Most hedges here want two to three trims a season, and we can put you on a recurring schedule or come back when you call. Price follows the count and size of the shrubs.

faq.q: Can you cut back an overgrown hedge hard at my Henderson house?
faq.a: Many hedges, like ligustrum and photinia, handle a hard rejuvenation cut and fill back in over a season or two. Timing matters, so we plan the cut for when the plant will recover best. We will tell you on the walkthrough if a shrub is too far gone and better replaced.

faq.q: Why are the bottoms of my hollies bare?
faq.a: Usually the top was sheared flat year after year, so it shades out the lower branches. We reshape the hedge narrower at the top and wider at the base so sunlight reaches the bottom. It takes a season or two to fill in, but it works better than trimming the same flat line again.

faq.q: How much does hedge trimming cost in Henderson?

faq.q: When should the azaleas and hollies be trimmed?
faq.a: Azaleas right after they bloom, because they set next year's buds on this year's stems within weeks. June is the clean window for hollies. We skip hard shearing in late fall, since tender regrowth burns brown in the first cold snap.

faq.q: Do you haul away the trimmings?

irrigation.local_h: Watering a Henderson yard that drains in two speeds
local: Henderson yards are sandy on top with clay underneath, so water soaks in fast and then stops. A system that runs one long cycle floods the low corner and leaves the high side dry. We run shorter cycles that let each zone soak in before the next one starts. That keeps the whole yard even and stops runoff from sheeting across the clay and onto the driveway or toward the foundation.

Older Henderson lots mix sun and shade in the same yard. A St. Augustine lawn under oaks and pines drinks differently from bermuda in the open, so we split sunny and shaded lawn into separate zones instead of watering them on one schedule. Slope, trees and existing beds get their own zones too. The walkthrough is where we look at how the yard really behaves, then write the layout and the price down.

Flower beds are the other mistake. Spray heads in an azalea or camellia bed soak the leaves, the mulch and the side of the house, and still leave the roots thirsty. We put beds and shrubs on drip, which wastes almost nothing and keeps foliage dry, which matters with the fungus that shows up in a wet, warm spring. Already have a system that is not working? We repair heads, lines, valves and wiring, on systems we put in and ones we did not, and we set the controller for the season. leaf-removal.local_h: Leaf season on an older Henderson lot
local: Between the oaks, pecans and pines on older Henderson lots, leaf season starts in October and does not really end until winter is nearly over. Sweetgums let go in the first half of November and the volume roughly triples in a few days. Post oaks and water oaks keep dropping into February, and pine straw keeps coming after the hardwoods are bare. So we plan passes for mid-November and mid-December, add a third for heavy canopy, and come back before spring green-up.

Most in-town Henderson lawns under big trees are St. Augustine, and that is the grass that pays for a wet leaf mat. It grows from surface runners and stays partly green into November, so every growing point sits right where the leaves land. A soggy blanket through a wet winter shades it out and sets up large patch. If you find dead circles in March, the leaves are often the reason, not the cold.

Azalea and camellia beds hold leaves like a net, and the leaves sit against the stems all winter. We blow them out of the beds and rock beds along with the lawn, re-edge the bed lines the leaves buried, and clear the drive, walks and patio. Exterior gutter clearing is part of the job too, which matters under oaks. The vacuum trailer takes it all away, so nothing is left in bags at the curb.

Out on the acreage, the pine woods drop straw all year and the distance to the road or drive changes the work. We blow everything toward a paved surface the trailer can reach, so the length of that haul is one of the things we measure on the walkthrough. The flat price you get in writing covers the passes we plan with you, and a post-storm cleanup after a big blow is quoted separately.

faq.q: Should I leave pine straw on the lawn in Henderson?
faq.a: Not a thick layer. A light scatter breaks down fine, but a mat of needles and leaves on St. Augustine through a wet winter shades it out and invites fungus. Clear it off the lawn and, if you like, use it in the beds under the pines. We will haul off whatever you do not want.

faq.q: How much does leaf removal cost in Henderson?

faq.q: When do you start leaf removal in Henderson?

faq.q: Can you clear the leaves out of my azalea beds?
faq.a: Yes. Leaves come out of shrub beds and rock beds, and we re-edge the bed lines afterward. We blow carefully around the plants and take the leaves with the vacuum trailer instead of mulching them into the bed, so you are not left with a mat of leaves against the stems.

faq.q: Do you leave leaves in bags at the curb?

mulch-installation.answer: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned, fully insured company based in Longview that installs mulch in Henderson. We are rated 5.0 on Google across {{REVIEWS}} reviews. local: Henderson has a mulch material that the trees supply for free. Under the pines, a pine straw bed fits the look of the yard and the trees keep resupplying it. Near the house, where you want a cleaner and darker finish, shredded hardwood is the better pick. Cypress, cedar and dyed black or brown are also on the list. We ask where the bed sits and what you want to see from the street before we choose.

Older Henderson beds usually have years of buildup. Mulch piled against trunks and siding holds moisture where it does the most harm, and a thick layer sheds light rain like a tarp. So the job starts with pulling old mulch back from the trunks and siding, re-cutting the edges and pulling weeds by the root. We loosen the crusted top inch of soil so rain gets down to the roots, then lay the new layer.

We keep the depth at an inch to an inch and a half. The three-inch figure on the bag is a northern spec for snow loads, and it does not fit our wet springs. Too deep holds moisture against stems until they rot and gives voles cover to eat roots all winter. For a 2,000 square foot bed, that depth takes about 8 yards instead of 19, so you pay for what the bed needs.

Beds against the slab are where Henderson water collects, so thin mulch and a clean grade matter there. We measure the beds, walk the edges, check how much of the old layer is left, and tell you whether you need a full install or just a top-dress. Late April through mid-May is the best window, and late September through October works for a thin top-dress before the leaves drop. That way you only pay for what the beds need.

faq.q: How much mulch do my Henderson beds need?
faq.a: Less than most people think. We keep mulch at an inch to an inch and a half over a clean, edged bed, since deeper than that holds too much moisture against roots in our wet springs. The three-inch rule on the bag is a northern spec that does not fit East Texas.

faq.q: Should I use pine straw or hardwood mulch?
faq.a: Pine straw suits beds under pines and gives a natural look. Shredded hardwood gives a cleaner, darker finish near the house. Both go down at the same shallow depth. We can also do cypress, cedar, or dyed black or brown, and we can bring bagged mulch where access is tight.

faq.q: What does mulch installation cost in Henderson?
faq.a: Most beds run $600 to $2,400. The price follows how many yards of mulch and how many beds we are refreshing. A fall top-dress over a layer that is still there usually costs a fraction of a full install.

faq.q: Do you put fabric under the mulch?
faq.a: No. Mulch should turn into soil over time, and fabric stops that. We pull weeds by the root, loosen the top inch of soil and lay the mulch directly on the bed. It is also one less thing to dig through the next time you want to plant or divide something.

faq.q: When should I mulch in Henderson?
faq.a: Late April through mid-May, after the spring growth flush and before the heat shows up. A second window is late September through October, when a thin top-dress goes down before the leaves drop and the first cold front comes through. A fall top-dress over mulch that is still there costs less.

retaining-walls.lede: Walls for driveway cuts, raised beds and lots that fall off toward a creek or the back fence, set on a real base with a drain behind them.
retaining-walls.answer: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned, fully insured company based in Longview that builds retaining walls in Henderson. We are rated 5.0 on Google across {{REVIEWS}} reviews. retaining-walls.local_h: Holding back the ground around Henderson
local: Retaining walls around Henderson do a few different jobs. Some hold back a slope along a driveway. Some wrap a raised bed. Others hold up a lot where the ground falls off toward a creek or the back fence. Each one has a different load, so we start by walking the site, measuring the grade change and finding where the water comes from. Then we spec the wall to hold what is actually there.

Water is what ruins walls here. Henderson sits on sandy topsoil over red clay, and clay swells when it is wet and shrinks when it dries. Behind a wall, that water has nowhere to go, so it builds pressure until the wall leans, bows and cracks. We put a gravel chimney and a perforated drain behind every wall, run to daylight, so that pressure never builds. A wall with no drain is a wall on a timer.

The base is the second weak spot. Sandy loam over clay will not carry a wall set on undisturbed dirt. We excavate below grade, compact a crushed stone base and set the first course dead level. Taller walls get geogrid. Segmental block is our usual pick because it locks together and flexes with the ground. Natural stone and boulder walls cost more but suit some properties. If a wall is tall enough to need a stamped engineering plan, we tell you at the walkthrough.

Short garden walls and seating walls start at a few thousand dollars, and tall structural walls run $20,000 and up, so height and length move the number most. A leaning or failed wall can be rebuilt. If a slope is already washing out, do not wait for the spring rains to make it worse. We build walls year-round, and a dry stretch is the best time to dig and compact.

faq.q: What retaining wall material works best in Henderson?
faq.a: Segmental block is our usual pick because it locks together, flexes with the ground and goes up clean. Natural stone and boulder walls cost more but suit some properties. What matters more than the face is the base and the drain behind it, and every wall we build gets both.

faq.q: How much does a retaining wall cost in Henderson?
faq.a: Most walls run $3,000 to $19,000, depending on height and length. A short garden wall starts at a few thousand dollars, and tall structural walls run $20,000 and up. Material, excavation, drainage and geogrid on taller walls also move the price.

faq.q: Does a wall need a drain behind it?
faq.a: Yes, always. Water behind a wall builds pressure, and in East Texas clay that pressure is what makes walls lean and crack. We put gravel backfill and a perforated drain pipe behind every wall, with an outlet where the water can actually leave.

faq.q: Can you fix a leaning wall on my Henderson property?
faq.a: Often, yes. A leaning wall usually has a weak base or no drainage behind it. We rebuild it course by course on a compacted base with gravel backfill and a drain. If it is too far gone to save, we tell you that on the walkthrough.

faq.q: Do you build walls on a lot that slopes toward a creek?
faq.a: Yes, and those jobs start with the water. We find where it comes from and where it goes, then size the wall, the drain and the outlet to match. Terraced walls can also step down a steep grade in stages instead of one tall wall.

sod-installation.local_h: Picking the right sod for a Henderson lot
local: Sod in Henderson usually comes down to the sun. Open lots and newer yards get bermuda, and we usually lay Tif419. The older neighborhoods with oaks and pines get St. Augustine, in Floratam, Palmetto or Raleigh depending on how much shade tolerance the spot needs. The mistake we see is bermuda in a shady yard because it is cheaper. In shade it quits, and under a pine canopy it thins to dirt by August no matter how it is fed.

Under about four hours of sun, no turf thrives long-term. On a lot with a heavy oak canopy we may tell you the back corner is better as a shade bed or mulch than a fresh pallet of grass. Before we quote, we walk the yard and note where the sun actually falls in summer, because that decides the grass, or a split of two grasses, for each area.

Prep is most of the price difference. Old turf and weeds come out to bare soil, then the grade gets set and two to three inches of compost or topsoil is tilled in, leveled and rolled. In Henderson that grading step matters. Sandy topsoil over clay drains fast and then stops, and flat backyards and low corners hold water after a storm. We fix the slope before we lay sod, not after it floats.

Timing is set by the grass. Bermuda goes down best from late April through August, and St. Augustine from May through September. St. Augustine needs four to six weeks of root growth before dormancy, so it should be in by the end of September. Water decides the rest. New sod needs a deep morning soak every day for the first two weeks, and we hand you that schedule in writing before install.

faq.q: When is the best time to lay sod in Henderson?
faq.a: Late spring through summer, while the ground is warm. Bermuda does best laid between late April and August, and St. Augustine between May and September. Sod laid in a dry July can work, but only with deep morning watering every day for the first two weeks. We set that plan with you before install.

faq.q: What does sod cost in Henderson?
faq.a: Most projects run $1,500 to $4,700, priced by the pallet based on the square footage you are covering. Patch repairs cost less. Large full-yard installs with heavy prep cost more, and the price shifts with the grass type, removing old turf, grading and how pallets can get to the yard.

faq.q: Which grass should I pick under my oak trees?
faq.a: St. Augustine, in a variety suited to the shade. Bermuda needs open sun and will thin out under a canopy. If the spot gets under about four hours of sun, no turf thrives long-term, and we will say so on the walkthrough instead of selling you sod that will not last.

faq.q: Do you prep the yard before laying sod?
faq.a: Yes, and the prep is the part that matters. We strip old turf and weeds to bare soil, regrade, till in two to three inches of compost or topsoil, then level and roll before the sod goes down. Starter fertilizer goes on at install.

faq.q: Can you patch bare spots with sod?
faq.a: Yes. We do patch repairs, plugs and full-yard installs. Before we patch, we look at why the spot died, whether that is shade, a low corner that stays wet or compacted ground, because new sod in the same conditions fails the same way.

tree-planting.title: Tree Planting in Henderson, TX: Oaks & Magnolias | Yard Dog

tree-planting.h1: Planting the next big tree in your Henderson yard
tree-planting.lede: When an older Henderson lot loses a big tree, the replacement should be picked for the next 50 years, planted at the right depth and watered through its first year.
tree-planting.answer: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned, fully insured company based in Longview that plants trees in Henderson. We are rated 5.0 on Google across {{REVIEWS}} reviews. tree-planting.local_h: Replacing a big tree on an older Henderson lot
local: Most tree jobs in Henderson start with a loss. An old oak or pine comes down in a storm or gets taken out, and there is a hole in the shade. We would rather talk about what goes there than just fill it. Pick for the next 50 years. Live oak, post oak and southern magnolia suit East Texas, and the right one depends on how much room you have, where the power lines and the house sit, and how much light the spot gets.

Where the old tree stood, the roots are still breaking down, and the soil there is often loose and uneven. We often shift the new tree a few feet off the old spot. We pick the location for the new tree's mature size, not for the stump's footprint. Then we dig a wide, shallow hole, set the root flare at grade, cut any circling roots and backfill with native soil.

Henderson's soil is sandy over clay, and a container tree comes in a ball of light potting mix. Until the roots grow out into the native soil, the tree drinks from that ball, and in July it can dry out in a day and a half while the clay beside it stays damp. So you get a written watering plan and a watering basin and mulch ring, kept off the trunk. On bigger installs we come back around the 30-day mark.

The best planting window runs from September to about Thanksgiving, and fall planting continues through February when we can fit it. A tree set in October gets close to six months of root growth before summer, versus about eight weeks for one planted in April. Out on the acreage, an open spot catches wind, so we stake only where the wind calls for it. We would usually rather plant a smaller tree that roots in fast.

faq.q: Can you plant a new tree where an old one came down in my Henderson yard?
faq.a: Usually, though we often shift it a few feet off the old spot where the old roots are still breaking down. We pick the location for the new tree's mature size, then plant it with the root flare at grade, a watering basin and a mulch ring kept off the trunk.

faq.q: What does it cost to plant a tree in Henderson?
faq.a: We do not publish a price because the species, the size at planting and the number of trees drive most of it. Site access, soil and drainage at the spot, and staking matter too. You get a written quote that includes the aftercare plan after a free walkthrough.

faq.q: Which trees do well in Henderson?
faq.a: Live oak, post oak and southern magnolia all suit East Texas, among others. The right pick depends on the spot, including soil, drainage, sun, room overhead and how close the house is. We walk it with you and recommend species that fit, not whatever is on a pallet.

faq.q: When is the best time to plant a tree here?
faq.a: Fall, from September until around Thanksgiving, with planting through February when we can. The soil stays warm after the air cools, so roots grow for months before summer. We plant year-round, but a spring tree needs more watering through its first summer.

faq.q: Should I buy a bigger tree so I get shade faster?
faq.a: Usually not. A smaller tree roots in fast and often catches up to a larger one planted at the same time, because a big one spends years recovering from the move. We would rather plant the right size for your spot and give it a good watering plan.

tree-shrub-care.title: Tree & Shrub Care in Henderson, TX: Azaleas & Oaks | Yard Dog
tree-shrub-care.meta: Tree and shrub pruning in Henderson, TX. Azaleas and camellias pruned after bloom, crepe myrtles thinned in February, small removals and haul-off. Free quote.
tree-shrub-care.h1: Pruning azaleas, camellias and shade trees in Henderson
tree-shrub-care.lede: Mature azaleas, camellias, dogwoods and oaks reward patience more than a hard hack, so each one gets cut in its own window and every limb is hauled off.
tree-shrub-care.answer: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned, fully insured company based in Longview that does tree and shrub care in Henderson. We are rated 5.0 on Google across {{REVIEWS}} reviews. We prune on each plant's schedule, thin crepe myrtles instead of topping them, clear dead lower limbs off shade trees and remove small trees and shrubs. Pricing comes after a free walkthrough, since no two Henderson yards have the same plants, and you get it in writing within a day.
tree-shrub-care.local_h: Pruning on the right calendar in an older Henderson yard
local: A lot of Henderson beds hold mature azaleas and camellias, and the calendar matters more than the saw. Both set next year's buds soon after they bloom. We prune them right after the flowers fade. A shear in fall or winter takes off the buds, and you spend the spring looking at a green bush with no color. Overgrown ones can be thinned back in stages, so the plant keeps its shape while it recovers.

Big shade trees on older lots tend to carry dead lower limbs that block light from the lawn and hang over roofs and drives. We clear those, and the grass under the tree thins out less. Oaks get special timing. East Texas has oak wilt, spread partly by beetles drawn to fresh pruning cuts in spring and early summer, so we leave oaks alone then and work in winter or late summer.

Crepe myrtles get thinned in February, before bud break, by taking out crossing branches, suckers and weak growth. We do not top them. A topped tree grows back taller on weaker wood, and a Natchez wants 25 to 30 feet however it is cut. If one has already been chopped, recovery takes two or three winters, so we plan it out and come back each dormant season to finish the job.

Small trees and shrubs that have outgrown their spot are part of the work, and so are storm cleanup and limb haul-off after a blow. We do not take down large trees near structures. Seasonal feeding for trees and shrubs and a mulch refresh around the base can go on the same quote. We walk the yard, flag what needs work and what should be left alone, and put the price in writing.

faq.q: When should I prune the crepe myrtles at my Henderson house?
faq.a: February, before bud break, and by thinning, not topping. Take out crossing branches, suckers and weak growth so the tree is cleaner and more open in the middle. Cutting every trunk back to the same knuckle each winter makes it grow back taller and weaker, not shorter.

faq.q: When do you prune azaleas and camellias?
faq.a: Right after they finish blooming. Both set next year's flower buds soon after, so a cut in fall or winter removes the flowers you were waiting for. If a plant is badly overgrown, we thin it in stages and tell you what to expect for the next bloom.

faq.q: Can you trim the old oaks in my yard?
faq.a: We clear dead lower limbs, but we keep oaks out of the spring and early summer calendar because of oak wilt. Beetles are drawn to fresh cuts in those months, so we work in winter or late summer. We do not take down large trees near structures.

faq.q: Do you remove trees and stumps?
faq.a: We remove small trees and shrubs that have outgrown their spot and haul them off. We do not do stump work, and we do not take down large trees near structures. The walkthrough is the place to find out which side of that line your tree falls on.

faq.q: How much does tree and shrub care cost in Henderson?
faq.a: We do not publish a price, because the work varies too much from yard to yard. You get a written, itemized quote after a free walkthrough, usually within a day. It follows the number of trees and shrubs, their size and condition, any small removals, and how much debris we haul off.
